subject: Tasmanian devil
title: Tasmanian Devils Catch Cancer From Each Other by Biting

scenes.text: Cancer can't spread from animal to animal. In Tasmanian devils, it does.
Devils bite each other's faces when they fight and mate.
Since the mid-1990s, those bites have passed on living tumour cells.
The cells came from one female devil's tumour. Her cancer now grows in the faces of others.
Once the lumps show, a devil usually dies within three to six months.
It has wiped out about 80 percent of all devils. The animal's own bite became the disease.

description:
Tasmanian devil facial tumour disease is a cancer that spreads like an infection: the tumour cells themselves pass from devil to devil through bites.
First noticed in the mid-1990s, it usually kills within three to six months of the first signs and has cut the devil population by around 80%.
Did you know a cancer could be contagious?
first_comment: There are now two separate contagious cancers in devils, called DFT1 and DFT2. Had you ever heard of a contagious cancer?
